problem:
The velocity $v$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
v(t)=⟨6t-1,{t}^{2}-1⟩.
$$

Given that the particle is at the position $r=⟨10,-1⟩$ when $t=3,$ calculate the position of $P$ at time $t=1.$

examples.knowledge_point: Calculating a Position Vector Given a Velocity Vector and Time
examples.problem:
The velocity $\mathbf{v}$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
\mathbf{v}(t) = \langle \cos t, \sin t\rangle.
$$

Given that the particle is at the position  $\mathbf{r}=\left\langle 0,\, 0\right\rangle$ when $t=\dfrac{\pi}2,$ calculate the position of $P$ at time $t=\pi.$
examples.worked_solution:
To compute the position vector, we need to integrate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int \operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t,\,\int \operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t+{C}_{1},\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{C}_{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $\mathbf{r}\left( \dfrac{\pi}{2} \right) = \langle 0,0 \rangle.$ Substituting $t=\dfrac{\pi}{2},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+{C}_{1},\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+{C}_{2}⟩ \\ ⟨0,0⟩ & =⟨1+{C}_{1},\,0+{C}_{2}⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

so we must have $C_1=-1$ and $C_2 = 0.$ Therefore, the position is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t-1,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and the position at time $t=\pi$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(\pi ) & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi -1,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ⟩ \\  & =⟨0-1,\,-(-1)⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
The velocity $v$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
v=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩.
$$

Given that the particle is at the position $(0,0)$ when $t=\frac{\pi }{2},$ calculate the position vector of $P$ at time $t.$
feedback.worked_solution:
To compute the position vector, we need to integrate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int \operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t,\,\int \operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{C}_{1},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t+{C}_{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $r(\frac{\pi }{2})=⟨0,0⟩.$ Substituting $t=\frac{\pi }{2},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+{C}_{1},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+{C}_{2}⟩ \\ ⟨0,0⟩ & =⟨{C}_{1},1+{C}_{2}⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

so we must have ${C}_{1}=0$ and ${C}_{2}=-1.$ Therefore, the position vector is

$$
r(t)=⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t-1⟩.
$$
